title: Annotatio I §.III cont: Passover instance applied to Hoc est corpus meum — same tropic hearing for the disciples
pass_a_gloss: The force of the consequence is tightened if this instance is applied to the Proposition of the Sacred Supper This is my Body — namely because Christ, about to institute and commend the Sacred Supper immediately after the Passover had been celebrated to disciples quite ignorant of the divine mysteries, could not have willed His words This, i.e. this bread is my body, to be understood by them otherwise than the words of the Passover just celebrated, This, i.e. this lamb is the passover or passage, had hitherto been understood by the same — especially when Christ added what is broken or is being broken for you, and in which sense the posterior Eucharistic proposition of Christ was to be taken: This cup is the N.T. in my blood which is poured out for you; Otherwise, and if either Christ had willed His words to be understood otherwise by the disciples, or the disciples had understood the same otherwise, Christ would have spoken to them quite obscurely, and a handle would have been supplied them for sliding into wondrous questions like those read in John ch. 14.
pass_b_english: Tighten the consequence by applying that Passover instance to This is my Body.
Christ was instituting the Supper right after Passover for disciples still raw in the divine mysteries.

He cannot have meant This bread is my body to be heard differently from This lamb is the passover / passage — especially with broken for you and This cup is the N.T. in my blood poured out for you — or else He would have spoken obscurely and opened John-14-style puzzles.
source_text: Adstringitur vis consequentiae si haec instantia ad Propositionem S. Coenae: Hoc est Corpus meum, applicetur, per id scil., quòd Christus S. Coenam immediàte post Pascha celebratum instituturus & commendaturus discipulis mysteriorum divinorum perquam ignaris, non potuit voluisse verba sua: Hoc, i. e. hic panis est corpus meum, aliter ab iis intelligi, quàm verba vixdum celebrati paschalis, Hoc, i. e. hic agnus est pascha seu transitus, ab iisdem intellecta hactenus erant, praesertim, cùm adderet Christus, quod pro vobis vel fractum est, vel frangitur, quôve sensu accipi debebat posterior propositio Christi Eucharistica: Hoc poculum est N. T. in sanguine meo qui pro vobis effunditur; Secus, & quodsi vel aliter intelligi verba sua à discipulis voluisse Christus, vel discipuli eadem aliter intellexissent, tam Christus iis admodum obscurè locutus fuisset, quam ipsis ansa suppeditata, ad miras quaestiones dilabendi, similes iis, quae leguntur Joh. cap. 14.

choices.english: the force of the consequence is tightened

notes: Passover→Hoc est corpus meum application; John 14 warning.
